summary: Validated randomized quiz draw (10 random questions per student) feature end-to-end. Backend pytest file test_quiz_draw.py created with 10 tests covering: PUT /modules & PUT /courses/{id}/final-exam persist draw_count; GET /modules/{id} returns exactly 10 shuffled questions (of a 15-question bank) stripped of correct/correct_multi (mc->single) ; same student receives the SAME draw on repeat GETs (persisted in quiz_draws); two different students receive different drawn question subsets/options; POST /modules/{id}/submit grades correctly against the student's drawn-and-shuffled options (answering the shuffled 'correct' index returns score=100, passed=true), submission documents include attempt=1,2,...; after failing, draw is deleted and a new GET returns a fresh random draw and the next submission is attempt=2; admin GET /submissions returns attempt field; final-exam flow: 403 before completing modules, 10 questions drawn without answers, failing returns course_reset=true, resets completed_modules/completed_tasks/module_results on enrollment, and subsequent GET /courses/{id}/final-exam returns 403; module without quiz still completable via /complete endpoint. All 10 tests pass (23.8s serially; 3.7s parallel). Frontend verified via Playwright: In admin course editor /cursos/{id}/editar the module edit dialog shows input `module-draw-count` with default value 10 and info text `module-bank-info` 'Banco: 15 preguntas · cada alumno recibe 10 al azar con alternativas mezcladas'. Evaluación final tab exposes `final-draw-count` and `final-bank-info`. On /evaluaciones (Submissions page) two generated submissions show badges `submission-attempt-{id}` with text 'Primer intento' (slate) and 'Segundo intento' (amber). Opening a submission reveals `choice-review` block with `review-question-i` and `review-result-i` ('Incorrecta'/'Correcta'); each option list highlights the Correcta option (green) and 'Respuesta del alumno' (rose), and the two attempts have options arranged in different orders (shuffle confirmed).
critical_code_review_comments: server.get_draw uses $setOnInsert so concurrent GETs from the same student atomically pick a single draw — good.

shuffle_options correctly remaps q['correct'] to its new index AND q['correct_multi'] after permutation; the stored draw retains the mapped indices, so auto_grade in save_submission grades against the drawn (shuffled) answers via get_draw() called inside save_submission (consistent with what the student saw).
strip_answers converts type 'mc' → 'single' for the student view — ensures frontend radio rendering is consistent.

After failing final exam, apply_result deletes ALL quiz_draws for that course (correct — forces fresh randomization on retry) and resets completed_modules/completed_tasks/module_results. Submission is marked course_reset=true. Response from save_submission includes course_reset — FinalExam.jsx correctly shows `final-reset-message` and `final-restart-course`.

Admin review (Submissions page ChoiceReview) uses sub.questions (the student's drawn-and-shuffled set) with their correct indices, so admin sees exactly what the student saw plus the correct option highlighted — matches user requirement.

Quiz pydantic model enforces draw_count>=0 but server also falls back to len(qs) when draw_count==0 via `n = draw_count or len(qs)`. Harmless but worth noting: admin cannot set 'use entire bank' via 0 without the fallback — currently works implicitly.

Minor: FinalExam.jsx line 18 — `shown` falls back to last_submission only for en_revision or when final_passed. If the student previously failed (course_reset=true), there's no last_submission because enrollment reset wiped progress state but the submission remains in db; however since module completion is wiped, require_enrollment+modules completed check at /final-exam returns 403 and FinalExam shows `final-exam-locked` with the backend error — correct UX.
Submissions.jsx AttemptBadge: fallback to 'Intento {n}' for attempt>=3 is reasonable; keep in mind the spec only names first and second intents.
